input.quote: MSL expressly warrants that all Products, MSL supplied materials and Parts, and work prepared for IBM will conform in all material respects to the specifications, drawings, or other descriptions furnished or adopted by IBM, and will be of specified quality, good workmanship, and free from defect subject to the following terms:
input.rationale: MSL gives an express conformance and workmanship warranty on all Products, materials, Parts and work (SOW 19.1(a)), with stated warranty periods in months for MSL Procured Parts (19.1(a)(iv)) and workmanship (19.1(a)(v)) running from delivery, expressly surviving acceptance testing and covering latent defects (19.1(b)) — i.e., at or above the preferred 12-month/90-day structure rather than the fallback. The remedy set is exactly what the playbook asks for and better: failure analysis, repair or replacement within a committed turnaround with MSL bearing return freight, and a refund of MSL's price (plus Parts prices) if repair or replacement is not possible (19.5), backed by an epidemic-failure recall obligation (19.7) and a title warranty (19.4). The implied-warranty disclaimer at 19.6(a) is limited to "other terms and conditions" and expressly preserves "MSL'S WARRANTY OBLIGATIONS DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION 19," so it does not swallow the express warranty; this is nowhere near the "AS IS" walk-away. Noted but not flagged as deviations: there is no separate "professional and workmanlike"/services warranty (subsumed in the good-workmanship warranty), no express compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty, and the specific period figures and the Section 16.19 survival cut-off are redacted ([*]) in this copy, so the numeric durations should be confirmed against the unredacted version. The clause runs in our favour as customer, so no redline.
